clue.text: Disreputable press cited for contempt

indicators.note: something disreputable is in a bad state, so the letters of the next words are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A scandalous newspaper is found in contempt of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disreputable' looks like a description of the press, but it signals that PRESS CITED is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a lack of respect is to treat someone with scorn.

clue.text: It's about time for a piece of news

indicators.note: about can mean in a different order, so the letters of time are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's about time' reads as the stock phrase, but 'about' rearranges TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is a single report or article in a bulletin.

clue.text: Primate replaces the ushers

indicators.note: read as re-places, places again in a new order, so the letters of ushers are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey stands in for cinema attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' is read as 're-places', putting USHERS in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is an Asian monkey, and monkeys are primates.

clue.text: Poet to serve as a good model?

parts.note: to serve as a model for an artist is to sit
well is the adverb of good

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a poet ought to pose for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was an English poet. 'Model' is read as a verb, to pose for an artist, with 'serve as a' padding the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell Sitwell were a literary family; Edith especially is known for her verse.

clue.text: Learning Heather goes out to work for a living

indicators.note: goes out means departs, so the word for heather leaves the first word

parts.note: the word is taken whole; that the answer also sits inside it is a coincidence, since the parse removes the heather word
ling is another name for heather

explanation.surface: A girl called Heather gives up her studies to get a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a girl's name, but it is LING, removed from LEARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain money by labour, so it means to make a living.

clue.text: For wrapping or handkerchiefs-its uses are varied

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: Thin paper has many uses, from parcels to runny noses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers both tissue paper for wrapping and paper hankies.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft thin paper is used both as gift wrap and as disposable hankies.

clue.text: Light and delicate piano had us quite excited

indicators.note: excited suggests agitation, so the letters of these words are stirred up

explanation.surface: A piano performance thrilled the audience with its airy touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaphanous fabric is so sheer and fine that it is almost transparent.

clue.text: It causes rough weather and loss of trade

definitions.meaning: a low-pressure system that brings storms

explanation.surface: Something brings storms and economic downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a meteorological low and an economic slump in business activity.

clue.text: Fish spear?

definitions.meaning: a long infantry weapon with a pointed head on a shaft

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a harpoon counts as a fish spear.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a freshwater predator and an old foot soldier's pointed shafted weapon.

clue.text: Shares exist in false teeth

indicators.note: the word for existing is placed inside the word for false teeth

parts.note: dentures are sets of false teeth
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A joke that investments can live inside a set of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: These are loan stock certificates issued by a company, loosely grouped with shares as securities.

clue.text: He wrote for various papers

indicators.note: various suggests a different form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journalist contributed to a range of newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: SAPPER was the pen name of H. C. McNeile, author of the Bulldog Drummond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The pseudonym belongs to a British novelist, so a writer is the definition.

clue.text: Letter that is spelt badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A note complains that a correspondence is poorly spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal written message, especially one in the New Testament.

clue.text: Creatures that ruin the mar rows

indicators.note: ruin means wreck, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Garden pests that spoil the vegetable marrows.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'marrows'; the letters of THE MARROWS are rearranged either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Annelid worms living in soil are small animals.

clue.text: One is certain to be this

definitions.text: One is certain to be this

parts.words: One is certain to be this
parts.note: reads as a statement of likelihood, but describes someone who is always right and never mistaken

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to be something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never in error is always sure of being right.

clue.text: We hear school meals should be this

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word for school is a sound-alike

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A view that school dinners ought to be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous boarding school near Windsor. The definition reads as 'what meals should be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals are meant to be consumed, so they should be eaten.

clue.text: Breaks faith and gambles about Ray

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for gambles goes round the name

parts.note: bets are gambles
the name is used as written

explanation.surface: Someone is disloyal, placing wagers on a man called Ray.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone is to be disloyal or treacherous to them.

clue.text: Should it be made from brush wood?

definitions.text: Should it be made from brush wood?

parts.words: Should it be made from brush wood?
parts.note: asks about timber, but describes a broom traditionally made of twigs, brushwood

explanation.surface: A carpenter wonders what material to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom of twigs tied round a handle, a brush made of brushwood.

clue.text: The ways of country folk

parts.note: seems to mean rural customs, but means the narrow roads that country people use

explanation.surface: A study of rural habits and customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanes are narrow rural roads, which are the routes country people travel.

clue.text: Craft lacking a prow?

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of the word craft is removed

explanation.surface: A boat with no front end.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the front letter, C, of CRAFT. The whole clue also defines a flat floating platform, which has no shaped bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a simple flat vessel with no pointed bow, so it fits a craft lacking a prow.

clue.text: One gentile about to become a Hindu ascetic

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
goy is a Yiddish word for a gentile

explanation.surface: A non-Jew turns into an Indian holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a practitioner of yoga, often an ascetic holy man in Hinduism.

clue.text: Singer gets an awkward note right

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy handling, so the letters of note are shuffled

explanation.surface: A vocalist hits an uncomfortable note but recovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges the letters of 'note'; the abbreviation for right then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a male voice part, and by extension a man who sings that part.

clue.text: Growing form of elation

indicators.note: a form of a word is a new shape of it, so the letters of elation are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elation is described as something that grows.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a nail on the foot keeps growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail on the foot is a growth that keeps lengthening.

clue.text: Still in a terrible fluster

indicators.note: terrible means in a dreadful state, so the letters of fluster are jumbled

explanation.surface: A person stays calm though in a dreadful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'nevertheless', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calm and quiet is tranquil and inactive.

clue.text: Can holy orders be so calm and peaceful?

indicators.note: orders as a verb means arranges, so the letters of the two words are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asks whether religious orders can be serene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holy orders' looks like the church phrase, but 'orders' is the instruction to rearrange CAN HOLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are ones of idyllic tranquillity, from the mythical bird that calmed the seas.

clue.text: Chinatown seems in confusion

indicators.note: in confusion means jumbled, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A busy Chinese quarter looks chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Chinatown' as 'china town': Meissen in Germany is famous for its porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: The German town gives its name to a celebrated porcelain, so it is a town of china.

clue.text: Having the flavour of the seasons

definitions.text: Having the flavour of the seasons

parts.words: Having the flavour of the seasons
parts.note: suggests seasonal character, but 'seasons' is read as seasonings added to food

explanation.surface: Something evokes spring, summer, autumn and winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with spices added carries the taste of its seasonings.

clue.text: Dress put on about spring

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for put on goes round the others

parts.note: clothes put on are on
a rig is a set of clothes, an outfit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dresses for the start of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan ran 'Dress' and 'I' together. 'about' wraps the word for put on round the outfit word and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring is a source, the place where something begins.

clue.text: Point-to point training establishment

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A college for a horse race over fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point-to point' reads as a horse race, but splits into two compass points around TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is a renowned English public school, a place where boys are educated.

clue.text: Mere colour

definitions.meaning: mere is an old word for a body of water

explanation.surface: Just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an inland body of water and a red pigment made from dye.

clue.text: If I tail car clumsily it would appear contrived

indicators.note: something done clumsily is messed up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver muses that following a car badly would look staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial means made or faked rather than natural, much as something forced is.

clue.text: Lose form in the heat

parts.note: sounds like a sportsman's slump in a qualifying round, but describes something softening into liquid when warmed

explanation.surface: An athlete falters in a hot qualifying race.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt is to turn from solid to liquid when warmed, losing its shape.

clue.text: People may have to put up with them

definitions.text: People may have to put up with them

parts.words: People may have to put up with them
parts.note: sounds like tolerating nuisances, but 'put up' means lodge, so these are the women who provide lodgings

explanation.surface: Some folk are simply an irritation to be endured.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who let rooms to lodgers are the ones lodgers stay with.
